title: Exact spectral-gap relation for the multi-urn backgammon model
statement:
Let $P^{(m)}$ be the transition matrix of the $m$-urn backgammon model and let $g(P^{(m)})$ denote its spectral gap. The model has $n$ balls distributed among $m$ urns, with the notation and dynamics defined above.

**Exact spectral-gap conjecture.** The inequality relating the $m$-urn and two-urn gaps is an equality:

$$
g(P^{(m)})=\frac{1}{m-1}g(P^{(2)}).
$$

Numerical diagonalization for the tested ranges of $m$ and $n$ supports the equality; the preceding argument establishes only the corresponding inequality, so the general exact relation remains unproved in the source.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0211166

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2002).
source_name: N. Destainville, “Bounding spectral gaps of Markov chains: a novel exact multi-decomposition technique”, arXiv:cond-mat/0211166 (2002).
